title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 761-762 of the 'suite à La Longue Marche'). Section 1° built, for a group G acting on a surface X with marked points S, an extension 1 → T_0^I → G̃ → G → 1. Here T_0^I is a product of copies of Z, one for each marked point. It comes from lifting the action on the circles S_i of tangent directions (half-lines) at the marked points to their universal covers. Mapping it to the Teichmüller group gives the 'special Teichmüller group' Sp T(X,S).

This page, section 2°, applies the construction to a local linear model.
- Definition (8): GL(2,R)^{±1} is the group of real 2×2 matrices with det = ±1.
- This group acts smoothly on C ≅ R^2 and fixes the origin. The 'circle of directions' S_0 at 0 (the set of open half-lines R^+ z) is identified with the unit circle U = {|z| = 1} via z ↦ R^+ z, as in (9).
- Under this identification, the induced action of u is z ↦ u(z)/|u(z)|, as in (10).
- One then lifts this action to the universal covering S̃_0. Take the base point s_0 to be the half-line through 1. The next page identifies the pointed universal cover with exp: R → U, t ↦ exp(2iπt).
- A lift of u_S is then the same as a choice of t ∈ R with exp(2iπt) = u(1)/|u(1)|, i.e. an argument of u(1).
- This yields the extension 1 → Z → GL(2,R)^{±1~} → GL(2,R)^{±1} → 1, as in (13). Over the identity component SL(2,R) it restricts to the universal covering 1 → Z → SL(2,R)~ → SL(2,R) → 1, as in (14). Next page: SL(2,R)~ is connected and homeomorphic to R^3.

On the det = −1 part, a lift reverses orientation of R, so conjugation acts on the kernel Z by −1. The extension is therefore not central over the whole group.

The crossed-out 'GL(2,Z)' in the title shows the purpose: to take the preimage of GL(2,Z) or SL(2,Z). This gives the special Teichmüller group of the once-punctured torus with a tangential base point, since SL(2,Z)~ ≅ B_3, the braid group on three strands. It serves as a model case for the general 'special Teichmüller group' extension by Z^I.
errors: Formula (10) as written, z ↦ u(z)/|z|, is a slip: for z ∈ U this is just u(z), which is not on U in general. The correct normalization is u(z)/|u(z)|; the next page indeed writes u(1)/‖u(1)‖.
Nothing on this page states that over the det = −1 component the kernel Z is acted on by −1, i.e. that (13) is a non-central extension. This is implicit and should be kept in mind.

ideas.what: Extension of GL(2,R)^{±1} by Z obtained by lifting its action on the circle of directions at 0 to the universal cover R; restriction to SL(2,R) gives the universal covering group.
ideas.modern_name: Universal cover of SL(2,R) (and of GL(2,R)^{±}, the 'arguments' or Poincaré rotation-number description)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Bargmann, Pukanszky; topological description via lifts of circle homeomorphisms, Milnor/Ghys)
ideas.where_published: Local model for tangential base points; cf. Esquisse d'un programme on T_{1,1}, SL(2,Z) and B_3 (unsure of an explicit treatment)

ideas.what: Using directions at marked points (tangential data) to define an extension of the mapping class group by Z^I, the 'special Teichmüller group'; the linear case is the local model.
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class groups of surfaces with boundary / framed tangential base points, the Z^n central extension by boundary Dehn twists (capping sequence)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in mapping class group theory (Birman, Harer); tangential base points in Galois-Teichmüller theory: Deligne 1989, Ihara, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, partial edition) discusses Teichmüller groups; the 'special' variant is unsure

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, explicit construction of the universal covering of SL(2,R) (and its Z-extension of GL(2,R)^{±1}) as a local model for the tangential-direction extension of Teichmüller groups. It is classical mathematics, and it serves the larger 'special Teichmüller group' discussion, whose ideas are themselves standard today.
transcription_corrections: Title: 'Les groupes GL(2,R)^{±1~}' with a crossed-out word; the deleted text looks like 'GL(2,Z)', and 'on pose' follows.
(10) reads 'z ↦ u(z)/|z|' as written in the manuscript (author's slip for |u(z)|), with 'z ∈ U' written under z.
'Nous relions de cette action ... une action sur S̃_0^# revêtement' is likely 'Nous relevons/déduisons de cette action sur S_0^# une action sur S̃_0^# revêtement [universel]'.
'u(S_0=1)' is likely 'u(s_0) (s_0 = 1)', i.e. lifting the image of the base point s_0 (corresponding to 1 ∈ U) to an element of S̃_0.
The symbol written S_0^# may be S_0 with a sharp/flat decoration; it denotes the circle of half-lines.
